title: Lost a python? Boston Animal Care and Control might have it.
author: Heather Alterisio
bullets: A ball python was found near Ellington Street in Dorchester, Boston, and is temporarily named 'Tippy.'
Boston Animal Care and Control posted on Facebook seeking the python's owner and asks for information to 617-635-1800.
City officials have not provided further details on the found python as of the latest update.

title: Tommy DeVito bests Drake Maye, and other takeaways from Patriots’ training camp scrimmage
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Team Blue, led by Tommy DeVito, defeated Team White 22-15 in the Patriots' training camp scrimmage.
DeMario Douglas excelled for Team Blue with six receptions and two touchdowns, contributing to their win.
Patriots wideout Romeo Doubs returned to practice after two days off for personal reasons, unrelated to injury.

title: A closer look at Harwich, voted the best town on Cape Cod by Boston.com readers
author: Kristi Palma
bullets: Harwich, a Lower Cape town, was voted the best town on Cape Cod by over 850 Boston.com readers.
Harwich features nearly 11 miles of tidal shoreline along Nantucket Sound and Pleasant Bay with over 20 beaches.
The town offers a variety of attractions including conservation areas, community centers, and daily oyster specials at local restaurants.

title: DA’s office says prosecutor’s ‘hot mic’ moment in Lindsay Clancy trial was misheard
author: Abby Patkin
bullets: The Plymouth DA's Office clarified that a prosecutor said 'shut it off,' not 'shut her up,' about autopsy photos.
Defense attorney Kevin Reddington accused prosecutors of inappropriate remarks during Lindsay Clancy's trial, which the DA's office disputes.
Judge William Sullivan issued a warning against inappropriate or disruptive comments in the courtroom after the alleged incident.

title: Little boy dancing to DJ on Boston Common has hundreds of thousands of new fans
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: 4-year-old Chukwuemeka Ikesinachi-Nwogwugwu danced to DJ music on Boston Common, gaining significant social media attention.
Chukwuemeka's dance video received over 200,000 likes and 4,000 comments, praised for his spontaneous moves.
The DJ event aimed at promoting human connection was led by DJ Miss S. Peace, encouraging the joyful moment.

title: Boston wine bar will keep its signature pours, just without the wine
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: Barcelona Wine Bar in Boston will serve porrón drinks with juice and soda after a three-day liquor license suspension.
The suspension followed incidents of serving alcohol to underage patrons and improper pouring of wine by a bartender.
The restaurant will enhance ID scanning policies and restrict porrón serving positions to prevent future violations.

title: Could Mike Vrabel keep 7 wide receivers on Patriots’ roster?
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Mike Vrabel is considering keeping seven wide receivers on the Patriots' 53-man roster this season.
Potential trade rumors involve Kayshon Boutte, who has impressed in training camp but could bring draft capital.
Kyle Williams, a 2025 third-round pick, is expected to play a significant role despite mixed training camp performance.

title: Suffolk DA candidates dispute ethics, transparency, experience at Roxbury debate
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Kevin Hayden, Rachael Rollins, and Linda Champion debate ethics and accountability at Suffolk DA forum in Roxbury.
The candidates dispute transparency in police misconduct investigations, with differing views on releasing body-camera footage.
Each candidate emphasizes their unique qualifications and experience for the role of Suffolk County district attorney.

title: What Boston meteorologists are saying about this weekend’s humidity levels, the potential for pop-up storms
author: Heather Alterisio
bullets: Heat Advisory remains in effect as temperatures reach near 90°F; feels like 100°F in parts of southern New England.
Pop-up showers and storms are possible Friday and Saturday evenings, with Sunday remaining dry but humid.
Humidity levels will be high throughout the weekend, with some relief expected starting Sunday into Monday.

title: Here’s some background behind the vintage baseball glove a Red Sox fan gave to Aroldis Chapman
author: Hayden Bird
bullets: Aroldis Chapman received a vintage 1930s Bob Feller model glove from Red Sox fan Andy Zides during a game.
Chapman, despite receiving the glove, gave up a two-run homer but Red Sox won against White Sox 12-11 in 13 innings.
The gifted glove pays homage to Bob Feller, known as an early flamethrower; Chapman holds record for fastest pitch at 105.8 MPH.
